title: Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 race for Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District features Democratic incumbent Seth Magaziner seeking a third term against two Republicans competing in a September primary—Victor Mellor and Stephen 'Doc' Skoly—and independent candidate Armando Anzoli. The district, which includes western Rhode Island and parts of Providence, has leaned Democratic and was represented by Jim Langevin for over two decades before Magaziner won the open seat in 2022 by about 3.5 percentage points. Magaziner, a former Rhode Island General Treasurer, has focused on economic development, healthcare, and veterans' issues, while both Republican challengers are campaigning on border security, affordability, and parental rights in education. The primary election is scheduled for September 8, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-June 2026. The race is rated as Solid Democratic by major election forecasters.

candidates.name: Seth Magaziner
candidates.summary: Seth Magaziner is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He previously served as Rhode Island General Treasurer from 2015 to 2023 and began his career as a public school teacher. Magaziner has focused on legislation addressing economic competitiveness, healthcare affordability, and federal workforce training during his tenure in Congress.

candidates.name: Victor Mellor
candidates.summary: Victor Mellor is a Republican candidate for Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District running in the September 2026 primary. A construction businessman who grew up in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, and later moved to Florida, Mellor is a strong supporter of former President Donald Trump. His campaign platform focuses on border security, deporting undocumented immigrants, reducing housing and energy costs, and refocusing schools on academic achievement. He has faced scrutiny over his presence at the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021, and past domestic violence arrests in Rhode Island and Florida that were later dropped.

candidates.name: Stephen Skoly
candidates.summary: Stephen 'Doc' Skoly is a Republican candidate for Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District running in the September 2026 primary. An oral and maxillofacial surgeon, Skoly previously served as Chairman of the Rhode Island Center for Freedom & Prosperity, a conservative think tank. He gained public attention for filing a lawsuit against the state after his dental practice was shut down for six months in 2021 due to his refusal to get vaccinated against COVID-19; the case was ultimately dismissed. His campaign focuses on energy policy, affordability, medical freedom, and parental rights in education.
